At its peak in the mid-1950s, the gap was roughly 45 to 50 percentage points. Gallup's 1956 polling had about 14% of Southerners approving of integrated schools, against roughly 60% or more elsewhere in the U.S. The gap then narrowed steadily, and by the 1990s approval was near-universal in both regions. These figures are from memory, so they may be off by a few points.

CONFIDENCE: 55
